absorption might be partly attributed to the inhibition of the b-carotene cleavage enzyme by lutein, shown in rats. b-carotene
also seemed to lower absorption of canthaxanthin, whereas canthaxanthin did not inhibit b-carotene absorption. Studies showed
that b-carotene increased lycopene absorption, although lycopene had no effect on b-carotene. a-Carotene and b-cryptoxanthin
show high serum responses to dietary intake compared to lutein. In addition, cis isomers of lycopene seem to be more bioavailable
